title: Control of East African Couch Grass in Tef

Header: Control of East African Couch Grass in Tef

Prevention: Seeds and fragmented rhizomes are presumed to be important in the propagation and spread
Only use certified seed to avoid introduction through contamination
Clean tools and farm machinery to prevent tubers being spread
Practice crop rotation with pulses and oil crops to reduce the esablishment
Monitoring: Perennial plant, with long slender branching rhizomes which form a dense mat beneath the soil surface.
Leaves flat, up to 15 cm long and 2-8 mm wide.
Inflorescences branched with 2 to 25 upwardly pointing, 2-11cm long flower heads ('branches')
Check in crop fields starting from one week after sowing for presence of this pioneer coloniser
Direct Control: Hand weeding at least 2 times starting from three weeks after sowing until the crop canopy formed
Deep tillage (>12cm) in order to disturb as many of the rhizomes as possible.
Do this under dry conditions so the exposed rhizomes dessicate
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Pyroxsulam (45%) at 400 mL/ ha to suppress weeds
L/ha on actively growing weeds before sowing controls them effectively
Prolific growth of annual broad-leaved weeds occurred where
D. abyssinica had been controlled with glyphosate these would need subsequent control
